faqs.q: How does casual loading affect a graduate teacher salary in Victoria?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for leave entitlements. For a graduate teacher salary Victoria, if you are employed casually, your hourly rate would be the base award rate plus 25%. For example, if the base rate is $35.00/hour, the casual rate is $43.75/hour. Super is then calculated on the casual rate.

faqs.q: Is super guarantee included in the graduate teacher salary Victoria figure?
faqs.a: No, super guarantee is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. For a graduate teacher salary Victoria, the employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary time earnings into a super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This is not deducted from your salary; it is an additional cost to the employer.

faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for a graduate teacher in Victoria?
faqs.a: The graduate teacher salary Victoria is set by the Victorian Government Schools Agreement or the relevant award. As of 2026, the starting salary for a graduate teacher (step 1) is approximately $78,000 per year, which equates to about $39.47 per hour based on a 38-hour week. However, this is an average figure; individual rates may vary by school sector and experience. Always check your specific employment contract or the Fair Work Ombudsman for award rates.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Graduate Teacher Salary Victoria: From Hourly to Annual

If you're a graduate teacher in Victoria, you might be offered an hourly rate or a salary. Knowing how to convert between the two helps you compare job offers and understand your take-home pay. This guide explains the conversion formula, the role of casual loading, and how super guarantee is paid on top.

### The Basic Conversion Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For full-time work, the standard is 38 hours per week. So if your graduate teacher salary Victoria is quoted as an hourly rate of $40.00, your annual gross would be:

$40.00 × 38 × 52 = $79,040

If you are paid a salary instead, you can reverse the calculation: salary ÷ (38 × 52) = equivalent hourly rate. For example, a $78,000 salary gives an hourly rate of about $39.47.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Most teachers are paid fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is your weekly pay multiplied by 2. Using the $40.00/hour example:

- Weekly: $40.00 × 38 = $1,520
- Fortnightly: $1,520 × 2 = $3,040

Knowing your fortnightly figure helps with budgeting and comparing to award rates.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) set by the Fair Work Commission from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week. However, graduate teachers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that almost always pays above the minimum. The Victorian full-time ordinary time average, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (May 2026), is $2,041.10 per week. This is an average across all full-time employees in Victoria, not the median for a graduate teacher. Your actual rate depends on your employer and classification.

### Casual Loading: What It Means for Graduate Teachers

If you work as a casual teacher, you receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (sick leave, annual leave). The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) is added to the base rate before any other calculations. For a graduate teacher salary Victoria, if the base rate is $39.47/hour, the casual rate becomes $49.34/hour. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator; always start with the base rate and add the loading separately.

### Super Guarantee Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid by your employer into a super fund. It is not deducted from your salary; it is an additional cost to the employer. For a graduate teacher salary Victoria earning $79,040 per year, the employer would contribute $9,484.80 in super (12% of $79,040), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means your total remuneration package is higher than your salary. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a graduate teacher earning $79,040, the estimated tax is about $13,417 and Medicare $1,581, leaving a take-home of about $64,042 per year. This is an estimate; your actual tax may vary with deductions or HELP repayments.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Using the Timesheet

To convert your own graduate teacher salary Victoria hourly rate, use [the timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading). If you are casual, tick the checkbox to add 25% loading. The tool will show your annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross, plus estimated tax and super. Always check your specific award or agreement with the Fair Work Ombudsman for exact rates.

### Summary

- Annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52
- Fortnightly = weekly × 2
- Casual loading adds 25% on top of base rate
- Super is 12% paid on top
- Tax and Medicare reduce take-home pay
- Use the timesheet for personalised estimates
